newsitem.title: UK: Stocks set records in London, Frankfurt.
newsitem.headline: Stocks set records in London, Frankfurt.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Wednesday.

LONDON - British shares set a record close for a second day, reassured as Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan denied trying to talk down Wall Street in last week's testimony to Congress, but unsettled by a sharp fall in gilts. With the markets still cautious ahead of further Greenspan testimony later Wednesday, the FTSE closed just 2.4 points higher at 4,360.1.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse trade at a record high of 3,364.99 points, buoyed by the strength of the dollar. The DAX-30 index ended up 44.33 points at 3,364.99. In post-bourse trade the index was up 30.36 at 3,375.45.

PARIS - Stocks gave up some earlier gains but still closed at a record after a rally underpinned by dollar strength and a rise on Wall Street. The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 14.50 points at 2,666.19 after an intraday high at 2,676.55.

ZURICH - Swiss shares set a record clsoing high, propelled by gains on Wall Street and in Frankfurt. Stocks firmed despite weakness in Swiss government bond futures. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) advanced 20.39 points, or 0.71 percent, to close at 2,890.83.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended sharply lower as unravelling of arbitrage-linked positions took their toll on the market. Trade was thin to begin with, which helped to magnify the losses. The 225-share Nikkei average closed down 291.27 points or 1.57 percent to 18,273.51.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong blue chips ended weak as interest rate concerns dampened sentiment in the market, but utility stocks moved higher, led by firm gains in Hongkong Telecom shares. The Hang Seng Index fell 39.32 points, or 0.29 percent, to close at 13,410.76.

SYDNEY - Australian shares closed just firmer with futures-linked buying in the afternoon lifting the market back to better than square for the day. The All Ordinaries index closed 0.9 points higher at 2,433.0.

JOHANNESBURG - South African gold shares closed 4 percent weaker depressed by a soft bullion price, which was hit by reports that the Swiss National Bank plans to sell some of its gold reserves. The All-share index lost 62.2 points to 7,070.4, the gold index was down 60.0 points to 1,432.9 and the industrials index dropped 35.2 points to 8,248.8.
